[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/27026173225607168 Brandon on Twitter - 17 January 2011]
On to The Great Hunt today. [http://twitter.com/search?q=%23Superstars #Superstars] slowed me down over the weekend, but I'm ready to jump back into it.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/27033222604922880 Brandon]
The EotW prologue is the series' best, but the one in TGH (the 'Darkfriend social' as fans call it) has always been a favorite too.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/27033344600440833 Brandon]
This scene is the first one that made me start to try to figure out who was a Darkfriend and who wasn't.

[http://twitter.com/SSingh03/status/27058502350409729 Shikha Singh]
There are no Ogier mentioned at the Darkfriend social. Does that mean there are no Ogier Darkfirends?

[http://twitter.com/SSingh03/status/27058502350409729 Brandon]
RAFO.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/27044807029293056 Brandon]
It's much discussed, but if you haven't noticed: Darkfriend social has Aes Sedai, then we learn Moiraine had been mysteriously absent.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/27045071085895680 Brandon]
RJ was very sneaky. This sent wot fandom into huge circles of wild-goose-chasing, many thinking Moiraine was a Darkfriend.

[http://twitter.com/BenVH/status/27056585377316865 Benjamin Van Hoesen]
Do writters really think about the fan conspiracy theories that much when writing? Seems like J. K. R. did a bunch. Do you?

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/27063683305705473 Brandon]
RJ certainly did. I do on occasion. Depends on the book.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/27057719676506112 Brandon]
"Most of the men at Fal Dara accepted Rand...some seemed unable to forget his being an outlander. Masema was the worst of those."

[http://twitter.com/Terez27/status/27062211490881536 Terez]
heh. Because Masema thought he was an Aiel! But yeah, the host of series-running characters introduced early...

[http://twitter.com/Terez27/status/27062485815140352 Terez]
...is well-played. Many in TEOTW, more in TGH. I have wondered if Bunt was RJ's choice or yours for 'Apples'.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/27083662885396480 Brandon]
Someday, I may answer that question.


[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/27083600050524162 Brandon]
Moiraine's plan was for Rand to take Illian first. She's the only Aes Sedai I know to say he needed to go off on his own for a while.

[http://twitter.com/cashadc/status/27130248424333312 Aaron Cash]
I have considered and contemplated this thought, I think Moiraine remembered that to truly control ''saidar'' you must surrender.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/27142001602334721 Brandon]
That's a very good way of looking at it.


[http://twitter.com/TankSpill/status/27027618360459264 Emil Schuffhausen]
I have 6 chapters left in EotW, should catch up by tonight. What scene are you most looking forward to in TGH?

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/27028670396768256 Brandon]
I love the ending. Probably that.


[http://twitter.com/wutdafuhk/status/27033901264277504 TJ]
While doing your [http://twitter.com/search?q=%23wotrr #wotrr], notice the metaphors. Loved RJ's style there. Not noticed in new book. Great though. 1/2 way so far.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/27043395046215680 Brandon]
Every time I try to do a Jordan-esque metaphor, I fail, so I remove it. It's an aspect of his style I can't imitate, I'm afraid.

[http://twitter.com/wutdafuhk/status/27046132198678528 TJ]
Aw man, I believe you're not giving yourself enough credit, but I'll respect it. Thanks again!

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/27049302522077185 Brandon]
I'll keep an eye on it. Maybe I'll figure it out. But often it's better to do things in my style rather than to poorly imitate RJ.

[http://twitter.com/Boethius32/status/27082820497186817 Jan Carrick]
Will you attempt to move closer to RJ's descriptive style in AMoL? You were close in TGS, but departed from that in ToM.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/27084946317254656 Brandon]
I'm afraid I knew from the beginning that I couldn't imitate RJ's style. I try in some ways, but I am not him.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/27085057835409408 Brandon]
I will write the book the best way I know how, but will not be trying to imitate RJ. I WILL strive for character voice accuracy.

[http://twitter.com/Boethius32/status/27133636465655809 Jan]
Well, the descriptive style is a central feature of WoT. I don't think being more descriptive would constitute imitation.

[http://twitter.com/Boethius32/status/27137905524744192 Jan]
I'm asking because your narrative style was much closer to RJ in TGS. I was surprised to see you move away from that in ToM.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/27142236865036289 Brandon]
Oh, I see. You don't mean "Describe in the way RJ did." You mean "Please describe more."


[http://twitter.com/dr_jekyll832/status/27067956219355136 Chris B]
Do you take notes, besides twittering, during [http://twitter.com/search?q=%23wotrr #wotrr]?

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/27083964715896832 Brandon]
Many.

[http://twitter.com/NFLHawk/status/27035076516646913 Matt H]
Can you put all of your notes online somewhere? Come on, that's easy...right?

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/27043607743561728 Brandon]
Lol. Those would have so many spoilers in them it would cause several people's heads to explode.


[http://twitter.com/FelixPax/status/27068536249647104 Felix]
What do you think of the literary method of foreshadowing by saying something is impossible to do or will not occur?

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/27084147101011968 Brandon]
I think it can work very well. RJ certainly did it quite a bit. You need to be somewhat subtle with it, though.


[http://twitter.com/SSingh03/status/27145736659410944 Shikha Singh]
Nynaeve knitting in Fal Dara is just not her. All later books are on how she can't sew and yet...

[http://twitter.com/SSingh03/status/27146059364958208 Shikha]
...in TGH she knits. Is there any explanation in RJ's notes as to why?

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/27214556086407169 Brandon]
There might be an explanation for that, but it would be buried so deeply that...yeah. I'll let you know if I happen across it.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/27214656300916736 Brandon]
Remember, though, there are three million words worth of notes.




'''''Non sequituri'''''

[http://twitter.com/TheAOster/status/27042704571502593 Aaron Oster on Twitter - 17 January 2011]
How could Verin write that note if she hadn't taken poison yet?

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/27045863050182656 Brandon]
An excellent question, one I'm surprised I haven't seen talked about yet. (Though I'm sure it has been.)

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/27045960991375360 Brandon]
Basically, it's for the same reason that an Aes Sedai can kill if she puts herself into a situation where she's in danger.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/27046297546530816 Brandon]
It involves mental gymnastics and lots of requirements. In the end, she put so many on that the note didn't get read.


[http://twitter.com/brianlep8/status/27062432006410240 Brian LePoidevin on Twitter - 17 January 2011]
Pardon me if this has been asked a million times but what did you find heartbreaking to write in ToM? Noal? Aiel future?

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/27064222097612800 Brandon]
Aiel future, all the way. And the death of a certain character related to Perrin.

[http://twitter.com/JeffEdde/status/27076141315530752 Jeff Edde]
Possibly a RAFO, but will you find aMoL to be even more Heartbreaking to write?

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/27084657971433472 Brandon]
It WILL be heartbreaking, if only because it's the last. I can't say if it will be heartbreaking for similar reasons or not.
